outcome_text: Apply classical measures of central tendency to summarise and compare data sets.
Calculate the mode for a given set of observations.
Calculate the mean for a given set of observations.
Calculate the median for a given set of observations.
Compare the mode, median, and mean, and justify when each measure is most appropriate to use.
Create and interpret a bar chart comparing group-level measures of central tendency.
Use empirical percentiles and quartiles to describe the relative position of observations within a data set.
Determine the first, second, and third quartiles for a given data set.
Interpret the meaning of a percentile in the context of a data set.
Determine the x percentile for a given data set.
Describe the relationship between the percentiles and quartiles of a data set.
Apply classical measures of spread to summarise and compare data sets.
Calculate the range for a given set of observations.
Calculate the interquartile range (IQR) for a given set of observations.
Calculate the sum of squared deviations for a given set of observations.
Calculate the population and sample variance for a given set of observations.
Calculate the population and sample standard deviation for a given set of observations.
